question: What makes an audience at a political speech burst into applause together, at the same moment?
answer: The speaker signals the finish line in advance. Studying hundreds of British party conference speeches, researchers found that contrasts, not this but that, and lists of three drew most of the collective applause. Both let listeners predict exactly when a point will end, so they can start clapping together instead of risking clapping alone.
move: Make the end of your point predictable and people can respond together.
ask: When I make my main point, do people know clearly when it has landed?
source: Heritage & Greatbatch, American Journal of Sociology, 1986
reference: Heritage & Greatbatch, Generating applause: a study of rhetoric and response at party political conferences, American Journal of Sociology 92(1), 1986
